title: Bioenergetics / energy balance (calorimetry, 4-9-4)
body:
Bioenergetics / energy balance (calorimetry, 4-9-4) — an engine domain that can touch it: nutrition. Calibration: seals — energy budgets compute directly. Food energy is measured by combustion: carbohydrate and protein yield about 4 kcal per gram, fat about 9, alcohol about 7. Energy stored equals energy in minus energy out — conservation of energy applied to a body, and not negotiable.

'ENERGY OUT' IS THE PART THAT IS MISUNDERSTOOD. Basal metabolic rate — the cost of simply being alive — is roughly 60-70% of daily expenditure; deliberate exercise is usually a small fraction. That is why exercise is excellent for health and a weak lever for weight, and why the arithmetic disappoints people who were promised otherwise.

AND THE TERMS ARE NOT INDEPENDENT, which is where the naive reading fails: reduce intake substantially and expenditure falls too, through lower BMR and reduced spontaneous movement. The equation still balances; the body simply moves the other side. Appetite hormones then push intake back up. The first law holds absolutely and is a poor behavioural plan on its own — both statements are true and the card keeps them together.

title: Exercise physiology (VO₂max, HR zones)
body:
Exercise physiology (VO₂max, HR zones) — an engine domain that can touch it: exercise_science. Calibration: seals — max HR estimates, zones and work rates compute. VO₂max is the maximum rate of oxygen use, the ceiling on sustained aerobic work, and the single best laboratory predictor of endurance capacity. It is also among the strongest predictors of all-cause mortality, which is why this card is about health rather than sport.

THREE ENERGY SYSTEMS, chosen by duration: phosphocreatine for the first ~10 seconds, anaerobic glycolysis to roughly 2 minutes (producing the lactate and the burn), and aerobic beyond that. Training targets one of them; a programme that mismatches system to goal wastes the effort.

HEART-RATE ZONES estimate intensity, though the familiar 220-minus-age formula carries a standard deviation of about 10-12 beats and should not be treated as exact for an individual.

PROGRESSIVE OVERLOAD is the whole principle: adaptation follows a stress slightly beyond the accustomed, then requires REST to occur — the gain happens during recovery, not during the session. Training without recovery is stress without adaptation, which is how injury and overtraining arrive.

title: Population ecology (Lotka–Volterra, carrying capacity)
body:
Population ecology (Lotka–Volterra, carrying capacity) — an engine domain that can touch it: ecology. Calibration: seals — logistic and predator-prey models compute. Unlimited resources give exponential growth, which nothing sustains. The LOGISTIC model adds a carrying capacity K, and growth slows to zero as the population approaches it — an S-curve rather than a hockey-stick.

LOTKA–VOLTERRA couples predator and prey and produces CYCLES, with the predator peak lagging the prey peak by a quarter period. The lynx and hare records from Hudson's Bay Company fur returns show this over nearly a century, which is a striking case of a simple pair of equations matching a long real series.

WHAT THE MODELS TEACH BEYOND ECOLOGY: OVERSHOOT is possible when growth responds slowly, so a population can exceed K and then crash below it rather than settling gently; and MAXIMUM SUSTAINABLE YIELD sits near K/2, not near K — harvesting a resource down to half its carrying capacity produces the most per year, while harvesting near capacity or near collapse produces little. Fisheries policy is this curve, and most fishery collapses are it being ignored.

title: Nutrient cycling & agronomy (NPK, evapotranspiration)
body:
Nutrient cycling & agronomy (NPK, evapotranspiration) — an engine domain that can touch it: soil_science. Calibration: seals — nutrient budgets and ET rates compute. Elements cycle between soil, plant, animal and atmosphere, and a farm is a budget: what leaves in the harvest must return or the soil is being mined. NITROGEN drives leaf and stem, PHOSPHORUS root and seed, POTASSIUM water regulation and disease resistance — the three numbers on any fertiliser bag, always in that order.

SOIL pH GOVERNS AVAILABILITY, which is why it is tested first. Most nutrients are most available between about 6.0 and 7.0; outside that range, elements present in the soil become chemically locked and the plant starves in the middle of plenty. Correcting pH can be worth more than adding fertiliser, and costs less.

EVAPOTRANSPIRATION — evaporation from soil plus transpiration from leaves — is the actual water demand of a crop, and multiplying reference ET by a crop coefficient gives how much irrigation is really needed. That calculation is the difference between watering by habit and watering by measurement, and in a dry place it is the difference between a harvest and none.

title: Agricultural science (yield, soil-pH suitability)
body:
Agricultural science (yield, soil-pH suitability) — an engine domain that can touch it: agriculture. Calibration: seals — yield, spacing, seeding rates and pH suitability compute. Yield is the product of plants per area, units per plant, and weight per unit — so a yield problem is always one of those three, and diagnosing WHICH is the first task rather than adding inputs blindly.

MATCH THE CROP TO THE SOIL BEFORE AMENDING THE SOIL TO THE CROP. Blueberries want pH 4.5-5.5, most vegetables 6.0-7.0, brassicas tolerate more alkaline ground. Changing a soil's pH is slow, expensive and partly reversible; choosing the crop that suits what you have is free.

WHAT MOST OFTEN LIMITS A SMALL PLOT, in rough order: water, then nitrogen, then light, then pH, then everything else — and Liebig's law says only the FIRST of these matters until it is fixed. SPACING is the commonest self-inflicted loss: too close and every plant is stunted, too far and ground is wasted, and the optimum is a published number for each crop rather than a matter of judgement. Timing to frost dates and day length costs nothing and decides whether the crop finishes at all.

title: Supply & demand / market equilibrium
body:
Supply & demand / market equilibrium — an engine domain that can touch it: economics. Calibration: seals — equilibrium points and elasticities compute. Price settles where the quantity people will buy equals the quantity people will sell. Above it, unsold stock pushes price down; below it, shortage pushes it up.

THE DISTINCTION THAT MATTERS IN PRACTICE is between a MOVEMENT ALONG a curve and a SHIFT OF one. A price rise reduces quantity demanded (movement); a rise in incomes, or a competitor closing, moves the whole curve (shift). Confusing the two is the commonest error in business reasoning — 'sales fell when I raised prices' may be either, and only the shape of the response tells you which.

ELASTICITY IS THE NUMBER TO KNOW: if demand is inelastic (necessities, addiction, no substitutes) raising price raises revenue; if elastic (luxuries, many substitutes) it lowers it. Whether to raise your price is an empirical question with a measurable answer.

PRICE CONTROLS DO NOT REPEAL THIS. A ceiling below equilibrium produces shortage, queues and black markets; a floor above it produces surplus. The intent may be humane and the mechanism is arithmetic.

title: Comparative advantage
body:
Comparative advantage — an engine domain that can touch it: economics. Calibration: seals — opportunity-cost ratios compute. Ricardo, 1817, and the least intuitive true statement in economics: two parties both gain from trade EVEN IF one is better at producing everything. What decides is not absolute skill but OPPORTUNITY COST — what you give up to make a thing.

THE PRACTICAL FORM FOR ONE PERSON: a builder who is also the fastest bookkeeper in town should still hire a bookkeeper, because every hour spent on books costs an hour of building, and building earns more. Being better at a task is not a reason to do it. This is the single most useful idea on this shelf for someone starting out alone and trying to decide what to stop doing.

It scales unchanged from a household dividing chores to nations trading, which is why it is on the floor rather than in a textbook chapter.

WHAT IT DOES NOT SAY, and the omission is where the argument is usually abused: the theorem shows aggregate gains, not that every individual gains. Adjustment costs fall on specific people in specific places, and 'the gains exceed the losses' is no comfort to someone in the losing column unless the gains are actually shared.

title: Time value of money & discounting
body:
Time value of money & discounting — an engine domain that can touch it: finance. Calibration: seals — present value, annuities and amortisation compute exactly. A pound today is worth more than a pound next year, because today's can be invested — so future amounts must be DISCOUNTED to compare them: PV = FV/(1+r)ⁿ.

COMPOUNDING IS THE WHOLE STORY AND IT RUNS BOTH WAYS. The RULE OF 72 is the field version: money doubles in roughly 72/r years, so 6% doubles in twelve. The same arithmetic is why credit-card debt at 24% doubles in three years if untouched, and why paying the minimum can mean paying for a decade. Interest compounds for the lender exactly as it compounds for the saver, and most people meet it first from the wrong side.

THE DISCOUNT RATE IS A JUDGEMENT, NOT A MEASUREMENT, and choosing it decides the answer. A high rate makes the distant future nearly worthless, which is how a spreadsheet can justify ignoring a cost arriving in thirty years. When an investment appraisal turns on the discount rate, the argument is about values and is only wearing arithmetic.

title: Modern portfolio theory (Markowitz)
body:
Modern portfolio theory (Markowitz) — an engine domain that can touch it: finance. Calibration: seals — variance, correlation and frontier points compute. Markowitz (1952): risk should be judged for the PORTFOLIO, not for each holding alone, because assets that do not move together partly cancel. Combining imperfectly correlated assets lowers total variance WITHOUT lowering expected return — the nearest thing to a free lunch in finance, and it comes from the algebra of variance rather than from any forecast.

CORRELATION IS THE ACTIVE INGREDIENT. Twenty stocks in one industry are barely diversified; a few genuinely unrelated holdings do more. Diversification removes the risk specific to one company and cannot remove the risk shared by the whole market, which is why the latter is the part you are paid to bear.

WHERE IT BREAKS, AND IT BREAKS EXACTLY WHEN NEEDED: the model assumes variance measures risk and that correlations are stable. In a crisis correlations converge toward one — everything falls together — so the diversification computed in calm conditions evaporates in the conditions it was bought for. Returns are also fatter-tailed than the normal distribution assumed, so the model understates extremes.

title: Double-entry accounting identity (A = L + E)
body:
Double-entry accounting identity (A = L + E) — an engine domain that can touch it: finance. Calibration: seals — the identity is checkable to the penny. Assets equal Liabilities plus Equity. Every transaction touches at least two accounts so the identity always holds; if it does not, something is wrong.

THE IDENTITY IS A CHECKSUM, and that is why the method survived 500 years. Luca Pacioli codified it in 1494 from Venetian merchant practice, and it works because a single-entry list of transactions has no internal test — an error is simply carried — while double-entry makes most mistakes announce themselves as an imbalance. It is error DETECTION built into the notation, which is the same idea as a parity bit or a checksum.

WHAT IT LETS A SMALL OPERATOR ACTUALLY DO: separate PROFIT from CASH. A business can be profitable and still fail, because a sale on credit is revenue today and money later, while wages are money today. Most small businesses that die, die of cash flow while showing a profit, and the two statements that would have shown it are the ones double-entry produces.

It does not stop deliberate fraud — both sides can be falsified together — which is why audit exists on top of it.

title: Labor economics (minimum wage, overtime law)
body:
Labor economics (minimum wage, overtime law) — an engine domain that can touch it: labor. Calibration: seals — wage, hour and overtime calculations compute exactly. Labour is bought and sold, but not like wheat: the seller must eat while negotiating, cannot store the unsold hour, and often faces few buyers.

THE SIMPLE MODEL SAYS a wage floor above equilibrium reduces employment. THE EMPIRICAL RECORD IS MIXED, and the reason is MONOPSONY: where few employers compete for workers, they set wages below the value of the work, and a floor can raise pay WITHOUT cutting jobs by clawing back that gap. Card and Krueger's 1994 study, and the large literature since, is why economists no longer answer this question from theory alone. This card exists to record that the confident textbook answer did not survive measurement.

WHAT IS NOT IN DISPUTE and is worth knowing concretely: overtime rules, misclassification of employees as contractors, and unpaid wage claims are the commonest ways people are underpaid, and they are matters of arithmetic and documented hours rather than of economic theory. Keep your own record of hours worked; it is the evidence that settles the dispute.

title: Real-estate valuation (cap rate, DCF)
body:
Real-estate valuation (cap rate, DCF) — an engine domain that can touch it: real_estate. Calibration: seals — cap rate, NOI and discounted cash flows compute. CAP RATE = net operating income ÷ price. A property yielding $12,000 net on $200,000 has a 6% cap rate. It is an inverted price-to-earnings ratio for buildings, and it lets two very different properties be compared in one number.

NET OPERATING INCOME IS WHERE THE LIES LIVE. NOI is rent minus operating costs — taxes, insurance, maintenance, management, and a realistic VACANCY allowance — and excludes mortgage payments. Optimistic vacancy and forgotten maintenance are how a bad deal is made to look good, and both are assumptions rather than measurements. Ask for the actual figures for the last three years, not the projection.

A LOW CAP RATE MEANS AN EXPENSIVE PROPERTY, which reverses most people's instinct. It can be rational — buyers accept lower yields where they expect growth or low risk — but it also marks the top of a bubble, when yields compress because prices ran ahead of rents. Compare the cap rate to the interest rate: when borrowing costs more than the property yields, the arithmetic only works if prices keep rising.

title: Contract theory & rule of law
body:
Contract theory & rule of law — an engine domain that can touch it: law. Calibration: map-only — institutional, not a computation. A contract is an enforceable promise, and enforceability is what makes trade possible between strangers. Without it, exchange is limited to people you know or will meet again, because the only guarantee is reputation.

THE ECONOMIC FUNCTION IS LOWERING TRANSACTION COSTS. When promises can be enforced you need not verify everything in advance, escrow every payment, or restrict business to family. That is why the rule of law correlates with prosperity more strongly than most natural endowments: it is infrastructure, as much as a road is.

INCOMPLETE CONTRACTS ARE THE NORM. No document anticipates every state of the world, so what matters is who decides in the unanticipated case — which is what 'ownership' actually means (Hart and Moore). Practical consequence: the valuable clauses are the ones specifying what happens when things go wrong — default, dispute, exit — not the ones describing the happy path.

A contract you cannot afford to enforce is a promise. Knowing which of the two you hold is the whole of the practical lesson.

title: Public choice / decision theory
body:
Public choice / decision theory — an engine domain that can touch it: governance. Calibration: map-only — specific voting paradoxes compute; the framework is interpretive. Apply the same assumption to public actors as to private ones: officials, voters and regulators pursue their own interests too. Not cynicism — consistency. Assuming self-interest in the market and pure altruism in government is an unexamined double standard.

CONCENTRATED BENEFITS, DIFFUSE COSTS is the workhorse result and explains more politics than any other single idea. A subsidy worth millions to twenty firms and costing each citizen a few pounds will be fought for ferociously by the twenty and ignored by the millions, because for each citizen the cost of paying attention exceeds the loss. Policy therefore drifts toward organised minorities, with no conspiracy required.

RATIONAL IGNORANCE follows: if one vote almost never decides an election, studying the issues is individually irrational even though collective ignorance is disastrous.

ARROW'S IMPOSSIBILITY THEOREM is the hard mathematical edge: no ranked voting system can satisfy a small set of reasonable fairness conditions at once. There is no perfect voting method — that is proved, not lamented, and it means the choice is between imperfections.

title: Game theory (Nash equilibrium)
body:
Game theory (Nash equilibrium) — an engine domain that can touch it: operations_research. Calibration: seals — equilibria of finite games compute. A situation where no player can do better by unilaterally changing strategy, given what everyone else is doing. Nash proved (1950) that every finite game has at least one, allowing mixed strategies — and the proof is a FIXED-POINT argument, so it guarantees existence while giving no way to find it.

EQUILIBRIUM DOES NOT MEAN GOOD. The prisoner's dilemma has exactly one equilibrium and both players end worse off than if they had cooperated. That is the central and most-transferable lesson: individually rational choices can produce a collectively terrible outcome, with no irrationality anywhere. Arms races, overfishing, price wars and pollution are the same structure.

REPETITION CHANGES EVERYTHING. In a one-shot game defection dominates; in an indefinitely repeated one, cooperation can be sustained because betrayal has a future cost. Axelrod's tournaments found TIT-FOR-TAT hard to beat: cooperate first, then mirror, and forgive quickly. That is a practical rule for dealing with suppliers, neighbours and rivals — and the reason communities that expect to meet again behave differently from crowds that do not.

title: Queueing theory (Little's law)
body:
Queueing theory (Little's law) — an engine domain that can touch it: operations_research. Calibration: seals — Little's law and standard queue formulas compute. L = λW: the average number waiting equals the arrival rate times the average wait. It holds for ANY stable queue, whatever the arrival or service pattern, which is remarkable for so simple a statement.

THE COUNTER-INTUITIVE RESULT IS THE VALUABLE ONE: waiting time does not rise smoothly with load, it EXPLODES near capacity. At 50% utilisation a queue is short; at 90% the wait is roughly nine times worse; at 99% it is effectively unbounded. The relationship goes as 1/(1-utilisation).

WHAT THAT MEANS IN PRACTICE: a system run at 100% of capacity is not efficient, it is broken, and slack is not waste but the thing that keeps waits finite. This is why hospitals at full occupancy collapse under a small surge, why a road at capacity jams from one braking car, and why a person booked solid cannot absorb one interruption without everything slipping.

VARIABILITY IS THE OTHER lever: irregular arrivals or service times lengthen queues at the same average load, so making service times CONSISTENT shortens waits even without speeding anything up.

title: Linear programming & duality
body:
Linear programming & duality — an engine domain that can touch it: operations_research. Calibration: seals — optimal values and shadow prices compute. Maximise or minimise a linear objective subject to linear constraints. Dantzig's simplex method (1947) made it practical, and it is one of the most used pieces of mathematics in the world: diets, blends, crop mixes, freight, staff rotas, refinery runs.

THE OPTIMUM IS ALWAYS AT A CORNER of the feasible region, which is why the problem is tractable — you need not search a continuum, only the vertices.

DUALITY IS THE DEEP PART AND THE USEFUL PART. Every LP has a shadow problem whose solution gives the SHADOW PRICE of each constraint: exactly how much the objective would improve if that constraint were loosened by one unit. That is a direct answer to 'what is my bottleneck worth?' — how much an extra hour of machine time, or another acre, or one more delivery van is worth to you, in the units you actually care about. It tells a small operator where the next pound should go, and it is computed rather than guessed.

It is also Liebig's law of the minimum made quantitative: the binding constraint sets the outcome, and duality prices it.

title: Reliability & tolerance stack-up (RSS)
body:
Reliability & tolerance stack-up (RSS) — an engine domain that can touch it: manufacturing. Calibration: seals — reliability products and RSS tolerances compute. Series reliability MULTIPLIES: a chain of 100 parts each 99% reliable is 0.99¹⁰⁰ ≈ 37% reliable overall. Adding parts makes a system worse unless each is far better than intuition suggests, which is the strongest argument for simplicity in anything that must not fail.

REDUNDANCY WORKS THE OTHER WAY: components in PARALLEL fail together only if all fail, so two 90% units give 99%. That is why critical systems duplicate — and why COMMON-MODE failure is the thing to hunt, since two pumps on one power supply are not redundant at all.

TOLERANCE STACK-UP: worst-case addition of tolerances is safe but wildly pessimistic, since every part being at its extreme simultaneously is vanishingly unlikely. ROOT-SUM-SQUARE adds them in quadrature (√Σt²) and matches reality far better, because independent errors partly cancel — the same reason random walks grow as √n rather than n. Designing to worst case costs money that buys nothing; designing to RSS without checking independence risks the case where the errors are correlated.

title: Structural statics (load, moment, floor-area ratio)
body:
Structural statics (load, moment, floor-area ratio) — an engine domain that can touch it: architecture. Calibration: seals — reactions, moments and load paths compute. Nothing accelerates, so forces and MOMENTS both sum to zero. From those two conditions the forces in a static structure follow.

EVERY LOAD MUST HAVE A PATH TO THE GROUND, and tracing it is the whole discipline: roof to rafter to wall to foundation to soil. A structure fails where that path is interrupted — which is why removing 'just one wall' can be fatal if it was carrying, and why the question to ask of any alteration is not 'is this strong?' but 'where does the load go now?'

MOMENT IS FORCE TIMES DISTANCE, which is why a cantilever is demanding and why a load near a support is far safer than the same load at mid-span. Bending moment in a simply supported beam peaks at the centre and goes as the SQUARE of span — doubling a span quadruples the bending — which is the single most useful proportionality in practical building.

DEAD load is permanent, LIVE load is occupancy, and environmental loads (snow, wind, seismic) are set by local code from local history. Floor-area ratio is a planning ratio, not a structural one, and confusing the two is a common error in reading a site's limits.

title: Network theory (routing, addressing / CIDR)
body:
Network theory (routing, addressing / CIDR) — an engine domain that can touch it: networking. Calibration: seals — subnet masks, address ranges and prefix matches compute exactly. An IP address is split into a NETWORK part and a HOST part; CIDR notation writes how many leading bits are the network, so 192.168.1.0/24 means the first 24 bits identify the network and the last 8 the host — 254 usable addresses.

ROUTING IS LONGEST-PREFIX MATCH: a router holds a table of prefixes and forwards using the MOST SPECIFIC one that matches. Nobody holds a map of the whole internet; each router knows only the next hop, and the path emerges from local decisions with no central plan. That is the design principle worth carrying — hierarchy in the addressing is what keeps the tables small enough to be possible.

HIERARCHICAL ADDRESSING IS THE SCALING TRICK: because addresses are allocated in blocks, a distant router can hold one entry for millions of hosts. Aggregation is what makes the system finite.

The practical field skills are the same arithmetic: choosing a subnet that will not collide, reading a mask, and knowing that a host with the wrong mask can reach some destinations and not others — the classic symptom of a subnetting mistake rather than a broken cable.

title: Cryptographic security (hashing, checksums, PKI)
body:
Cryptographic security (hashing, checksums, PKI) — an engine domain that can touch it: cybersecurity. Calibration: seals — digests and signatures verify exactly. Three different things people routinely confuse. A HASH is one-way: any input gives a fixed-size digest, the same input always gives the same digest, and the input cannot be recovered. A CHECKSUM detects accidental corruption but not deliberate tampering. ENCRYPTION is reversible with a key. Hashing is NOT encryption, and a password stored 'encrypted' is stored badly.

PUBLIC-KEY CRYPTOGRAPHY separates the key that locks from the key that unlocks. Publish one, keep the other, and two people who have never met can communicate privately — or one can SIGN something so anyone can verify it came from the holder of the private key and was not altered. That signature property is what this project runs on: a seal anyone can check without holding our secret.

THE HONEST CAVEAT: the security rests on problems BELIEVED hard, not proved hard. If P = NP, or when a large quantum computer runs Shor's algorithm, factoring-based schemes fall. Hash functions do fail in practice — MD5 and SHA-1 are broken for collision resistance and must not be trusted for signatures. Cryptography is a moving floor, and 'we used encryption' is not a security claim without saying which, and how the keys are held.

title: Sabermetrics / sports analytics (Pythagorean expectation, Elo)
body:
Sabermetrics / sports analytics (Pythagorean expectation, Elo) — an engine domain that can touch it: sports_analytics. Calibration: seals — expected win ratios and Elo updates compute. Bill James's Pythagorean expectation: expected win fraction = runs scored² / (runs scored² + runs allowed²). It predicts a season's record from run differential MORE accurately than the actual win-loss record predicts the next season — which is the whole finding in one sentence.

A team beating its Pythagorean expectation is usually LUCKY in close games rather than clutch, and will regress. Separating the signal (run differential) from the noisy outcome (wins) is a general skill, and sport is the cleanest laboratory for it because the data are complete and the outcomes unambiguous.

ELO IS A BAYESIAN UPDATE IN DISGUISE. Each player or team holds a rating; the difference predicts the win probability by a logistic curve; and after each result both ratings move by an amount proportional to the SURPRISE — beating a favourite moves you far more than beating a weak opponent, and an expected result barely moves anything. Devised by Arpad Elo for chess, it now rates football teams, video-game players and language models, because it needs only pairwise outcomes and no absolute scale.

THE TRANSFERABLE DISCIPLINE: measure what PREDICTS rather than what is traditionally counted, prefer rates to totals, and expect extremes to regress. The resistance sabermetrics met — scouts insisting judgement beat counting — is what any measurement meets when it contradicts an expert's intuition, and it is settled the same way: check which one predicts.

title: Photographic exposure theory (exposure value, reciprocity)
body:
Photographic exposure theory (exposure value, reciprocity) — an engine domain that can touch it: photography. Calibration: seals — exposure values and equivalent settings compute. Three controls set how much light reaches the sensor: APERTURE (how wide the opening), SHUTTER SPEED (how long it is open), and ISO (how strongly the signal is amplified). Exposure value combines them into one number.

RECIPROCITY is the working rule: halving one and doubling another leaves exposure unchanged, so f/8 at 1/125 equals f/11 at 1/60. Each doubling is one STOP, and stops are the common unit for all three controls — which is what makes them tradeable.

BUT THE TRADES ARE NOT EQUIVALENT IN THE PICTURE, and that is the actual craft. Aperture also sets DEPTH OF FIELD (wide open blurs the background); shutter speed also sets MOTION (slow blurs movement, and roughly 1/focal-length is the limit for hand-holding); ISO also sets NOISE. You are never choosing exposure alone — you are choosing which side effect you want, and the exposure follows.

The same three-way trade with a fixed product appears wherever a quantity is set by several multiplicative factors, which is why this card sits on a floor with queueing and reliability rather than in a hobby manual.

title: Structural & generative linguistics (Saussure, Chomsky)
body:
Structural & generative linguistics (Saussure, Chomsky) — an engine domain that can touch it: linguistics. Calibration: map-only — interpretive; specific phonological and syntactic rules compute. SAUSSURE: the linguistic sign joins a sound-image to a concept, and the link is ARBITRARY — nothing about a tree requires the sound 'tree'. Meaning arises from DIFFERENCE within a system rather than from resemblance to the world, which is why a word's sense shifts when a neighbouring word appears or disappears.

CHOMSKY: syntax is generative — a finite set of rules producing unlimited novel sentences, which is why you can understand a sentence never spoken before. His argument from the POVERTY OF THE STIMULUS holds that children acquire grammar too fast and too uniformly, on too little and too noisy input, for pure induction to explain, implying innate structure. It is contested — usage-based accounts argue the input is richer than claimed — and the card records the dispute rather than settling it.

WHY IT MATTERS TO THIS PROJECT: if meaning is systemic and syntax generative, then translation is never word-for-word substitution, and a concordance must index SENSE in context rather than string matches alone.

title: Music theory (harmonic series, equal temperament)
body:
Music theory (harmonic series, equal temperament) — an engine domain that can touch it: music_theory. Calibration: seals — frequencies, intervals and temperament errors compute exactly. A vibrating string sounds a fundamental plus integer multiples of it. Simple frequency ratios share overtones and sound consonant: octave 2:1, perfect fifth 3:2, fourth 4:3. This is arithmetic that the ear performs, and it is why the same intervals appear in unrelated musical cultures.

THE PROBLEM THAT FORCED A COMPROMISE: stack twelve perfect fifths and you do not land on a whole number of octaves. (3/2)¹² is about 129.75 while 2⁷ is 128 — the PYTHAGOREAN COMMA, a gap of roughly a quarter semitone. Pure intervals and a closed twelve-note system are mathematically incompatible, and no tuning can have both.

EQUAL TEMPERAMENT resolves it by detuning every fifth very slightly, making each semitone exactly the twelfth root of two. Every key becomes equally usable and every interval except the octave becomes slightly impure. It is the clearest case on this floor of a deliberate, quantified compromise adopted because the exact solution is impossible — and the fifth is off by only about 2 cents, which almost no one hears.

title: Aristotelian rhetoric & fallacy taxonomy
body:
Aristotelian rhetoric & fallacy taxonomy — an engine domain that can touch it: rhetoric. Calibration: map-only — interpretive; fallacy identification is checkable. Aristotle's three appeals: ETHOS (the speaker's credibility), PATHOS (the audience's emotion), LOGOS (the argument itself). His claim is descriptive rather than cynical — persuasion works through all three whether or not the speaker intends it, so the honest course is to know which one is doing the work.

THE FALLACY TAXONOMY IS A DEFENSIVE INSTRUMENT: ad hominem attacks the person instead of the claim; straw man refutes a weaker version than was offered; false dilemma presents two options where more exist; appeal to authority substitutes a name for a reason; begging the question assumes the conclusion. Naming these is what lets you resist an argument that FEELS convincing.

A CAUTION THE CARD KEEPS: identifying a fallacy shows the argument fails, not that the conclusion is false — treating 'that was a fallacy' as 'therefore you are wrong' is itself an error. And an argument can be entirely valid and still be aimed at something untrue, which is why rhetoric sits beside logic on this floor rather than instead of it.

title: Formal logic & epistemology (validity, inference)
body:
Formal logic & epistemology (validity, inference) — an engine domain that can touch it: philosophy. Calibration: map-only — validity checks compute; epistemology is interpretive. VALIDITY and TRUTH are different properties, and confusing them is the most consequential error in reasoning. A valid argument guarantees that IF the premises are true the conclusion must be; it says nothing about whether they are. An argument is SOUND only when it is valid AND its premises are true. Perfectly valid reasoning from false premises produces confident nonsense.

THREE KINDS OF INFERENCE, and only one is certain. DEDUCTION preserves truth and adds no information. INDUCTION generalises from cases and can always fail — Hume's problem, still unsolved. ABDUCTION infers the best available explanation and is what diagnosis, detective work and most science actually use, while being the weakest of the three.

KNOWLEDGE was long defined as justified true belief until Gettier (1963) produced cases satisfying all three that nobody would call knowledge. Fifty years of proposed repairs have not settled it. This project's own posture follows from that: state the warrant, distinguish CONFIRMED from PLAUSIBLE from RESONANCE, and never let a valid-looking chain substitute for a checked premise.

title: Normative ethics (consequentialism / deontology / virtue)
body:
Normative ethics (consequentialism / deontology / virtue) — an engine domain that can touch it: philosophy. Calibration: map-only — interpretive by nature, and the card says so plainly. Three families of answer to 'what makes an act right'. CONSEQUENTIALISM: outcomes — the greatest good, however counted. DEONTOLOGY: duties and rights — some acts are forbidden whatever the result. VIRTUE ETHICS: character — what a person of practical wisdom would do, and what the act makes of the actor.

EACH HAS A COST THAT IS NOT A CARICATURE. Consequentialism can license atrocity for a large enough calculated benefit and requires predicting outcomes nobody can predict. Deontology can bind you to a rule while disaster follows, and its rules conflict with one another. Virtue ethics gives the least action-guidance when you most need it — telling you to be courageous without telling you what to do.

MOST PEOPLE USE ALL THREE and switch without noticing, which is worth knowing about yourself. This card is deliberately map-only: an engine can check an argument's VALIDITY and can retrieve what each tradition holds, and it cannot adjudicate between them. Refusing to pretend otherwise is the position — the judgement belongs to a person who will bear the consequences.

title: Calendar theory (Gregorian reform, leap rules)
body:
Calendar theory (Gregorian reform, leap rules) — an engine domain that can touch it: calendar_time. Calibration: seals — leap rules and date arithmetic compute exactly. The tropical year is about 365.2422 days — not a whole number, and not exactly 365.25 either. The Julian calendar's simple every-fourth-year rule overshot by roughly 11 minutes a year, which is a day every 128 years and about ten days by the sixteenth century.

THE GREGORIAN RULE (1582) fixes it with an exception to the exception: leap years are divisible by 4, EXCEPT centuries, EXCEPT centuries divisible by 400. So 1900 was not a leap year and 2000 was. That gives 365.2425 days, accurate to about one day in 3,000 years.

TEN DAYS WERE DELETED to realign the date — 4 October 1582 was followed by 15 October — and adoption took centuries, with Britain and its colonies waiting until 1752 and dropping eleven. Historical dates from that period are genuinely ambiguous unless the calendar is specified, which is why chronology software must carry the system with the date.

The lesson generalises: when a natural period does not divide evenly, you must choose your error and schedule its correction. Every leap rule, in any system, is that choice written down.

title: Historical chronology (era reckoning, elapsed years)
body:
Historical chronology (era reckoning, elapsed years) — an engine domain that can touch it: history_chronology. Calibration: seals — elapsed-year arithmetic computes exactly. Placing events on one timeline when the sources count from different origins: regnal years, Olympiads, AUC from Rome's founding, the Hebrew calendar, the Hijri calendar, and BC/AD or BCE/CE.

THERE IS NO YEAR ZERO in the conventional Christian era — 1 BC is followed directly by AD 1 — so elapsed time across the boundary is one less than naive subtraction. From 5 BC to AD 5 is nine years, not ten. Astronomers use a year 0 precisely to avoid this, which means astronomical and historical year numbers DIFFER before AD 1 and must never be mixed.

OTHER TRAPS THAT MATTER: the Hijri calendar is lunar and its year is about 354 days, so it drifts against the solar year by roughly 11 days annually and cannot be converted by adding a constant. Regnal dating requires knowing whether a partial first year counted. And the Gregorian changeover means the same day carries two dates depending on the country.

Dates are DERIVED quantities carrying assumptions, not raw facts — which is why a chronology should state its system alongside its numbers.

title: Fixed-point theorems (Brouwer, Kakutani)
body:
Fixed-point theorems (Brouwer, Kakutani) — an engine domain that can touch it: mathematics. Calibration: map-only — an existence proof, not a computation. Brouwer: any continuous map of a convex compact set into itself leaves at least one point unmoved. Kakutani extends this to set-valued maps.

THE HOMELY VERSION: stir a cup of coffee and at least one molecule ends where it began; crumple a map and lay it on the original and some point lies exactly over itself.

IT IS PURE TOPOLOGY DOING ECONOMIC AND PHYSICAL WORK. Nash's proof that an equilibrium exists in every finite game is a Kakutani argument, and von Neumann's minimax rests on Brouwer — which is why economics can assert an equilibrium EXISTS while being unable to say where it is. These theorems are non-constructive: they guarantee the point and give no method to find it, and that gap between existence and construction is itself a recurring feature of the floor.

title: Quantum information & entanglement (von Neumann entropy)
body:
Quantum information & entanglement (von Neumann entropy) — an engine domain that can touch it: information_theory. Calibration: seals. S = -Tr(ρ log ρ), the entropy of a density matrix, which reduces EXACTLY to Shannon's H = -Σ p log p in the eigenbasis — the same functional, one door further in.

WHAT IS GENUINELY NEW rather than classical information in new clothes: the NO-CLONING theorem says an unknown quantum state cannot be copied, which is why quantum key distribution can detect an eavesdropper rather than merely deter one. Entanglement is a resource that can be quantified and spent — teleportation and superdense coding are exchange rates between entanglement and classical bits.

THE THREAT IT CARRIES IS ALSO REAL: Shor's algorithm factors in polynomial time on a quantum computer, so the hardness that public-key cryptography rests on is a claim about CLASSICAL machines only.

title: Evolutionary game theory (evolutionarily stable strategies)
body:
Evolutionary game theory (evolutionarily stable strategies) — an engine domain that can touch it: biology. Calibration: map-only — stability conditions compute; the biology is empirical. Maynard Smith's ESS: a strategy that, once common, cannot be invaded by any rare mutant. It is a Nash equilibrium with a stability requirement added — and crucially, REPRODUCTION does the choosing rather than reasoning, so no rationality or foresight is assumed anywhere.

THAT IS WHY IT TRAVELS SO FAR. Game theory usually needs players who calculate; this version needs only differential survival, so it applies to bacteria, plants and hearts as readily as to people. Hawk-Dove explains why conflicts are often settled by display rather than by fighting to the death: an all-aggression population is invadable, and the stable outcome is a MIX.

IT ALSO EXPLAINS COOPERATION WITHOUT ALTRUISM. Kin selection (Hamilton's rule: help when relatedness times benefit exceeds cost) and reciprocal altruism in repeated encounters both produce genuinely cooperative behaviour from selection alone. Sex ratios settling near 1:1, the mix of aggressive and cautious strategies in a population — these are equilibria, not choices.

title: Control theory & cybernetics (feedback, stability)
body:
Control theory & cybernetics (feedback, stability) — an engine domain that can touch it: operations_research. Calibration: partial — stability criteria and PID responses compute. Steer a system by the DIFFERENCE between where it is and where it should be. Sensor, comparator, controller, actuator, and the loop closes back on itself — the same diagram whether the system is a thermostat, a governor, a body's temperature, or a business adjusting to demand.

STABILITY IS A PROPERTY OF THE LOOP, NOT OF THE PARTS. Good components in a badly designed loop oscillate or run away, and the mathematics is eigenvalues: a linear system is stable exactly when the eigenvalues of its state matrix lie in the left half-plane.

DELAY IS THE ENEMY. A loop that responds to old information overshoots, then overcorrects, and oscillates — which is the shower where the hot water arrives too late, the supply chain that swings between shortage and glut (the bullwhip effect), and the policy that arrives after the recession it was meant to prevent. GAIN too high does the same.

PID is the workhorse: respond to the present error, to its accumulation, and to its rate of change. Nearly all industrial control is these three terms tuned against each other.

title: Dynamical systems & deterministic chaos
body:
Dynamical systems & deterministic chaos — an engine domain that can touch it: mathematics. Calibration: map-only — sensitivity is qualitative; specific trajectories compute. Deterministic rules whose outcomes cannot be predicted: arbitrarily small differences in starting conditions grow exponentially, at a rate given by the Lyapunov exponent. Lorenz found it in 1963 when a weather run restarted from a printout rounded to three decimals diverged completely from the original.

DETERMINISTIC AND UNPREDICTABLE ARE COMPATIBLE, and this card exists to keep those two words apart. The system has no randomness in it; the limit is on KNOWLEDGE of the initial state, which is always finite. Consequences are practical and permanent: weather forecasts degrade past about two weeks regardless of computing power, and the solar system itself is chaotic on ~5-million-year timescales, so ephemeris prediction has a horizon no instrument removes.

title: Computational complexity (P, NP, reductions)
body:
Computational complexity (P, NP, reductions) — an engine domain that can touch it: computer_science. Calibration: map-only — P vs NP is open, and this card says so. Not whether a problem can be solved but how expensively. P is what is solvable in polynomial time; NP is what can be VERIFIED in polynomial time. Whether P = NP is unsolved and carries a Clay Millennium Prize.

REDUCTION IS THE TOOL AND THE INSIGHT: Cook and Levin (1971) showed that certain NP problems are universal — solve one efficiently and you solve them all. Thousands of practical problems, from scheduling to routing to protein folding, are now known to be NP-complete, which means they are the same problem wearing different clothes.

The honest statement for this floor: nearly all public-key cryptography rests on problems BELIEVED hard, not proved hard. If P = NP, that security evaporates. We are standing on a conjecture and should name it.

title: Fourier analysis & signal processing
body:
Fourier analysis & signal processing — an engine domain that can touch it: mathematics. Calibration: seals. Any well-behaved signal is a sum of sinusoids, and the transform moves freely between the time view and the frequency view of the same object. Fourier introduced it in 1822 to solve heat flow, and it was resisted as insufficiently rigorous.

THE UNCERTAINTY IS BUILT INTO THE MATHEMATICS: a signal narrow in time is necessarily broad in frequency. That single fact governs radar resolution, the attack of a musical note, the bandwidth of a radio channel, and — with ħ supplying the scale — Heisenberg's principle, which is the same theorem about conjugate variables rather than a separate physical mystery.

NYQUIST–SHANNON sets the practical floor: sample at more than twice the highest frequency present and the original is recoverable exactly; sample slower and aliasing folds high frequencies down onto low ones irreversibly. Every digital recording ever made obeys this line.

title: Measure theory (Lebesgue integration)
body:
Measure theory (Lebesgue integration) — an engine domain that can touch it: mathematics. Calibration: map-only — a foundation, not a computation. What it means for a set to have a SIZE, done carefully enough to survive infinity. Riemann integration slices the domain vertically; Lebesgue slices by VALUE, asking how much of the domain maps to each height — the difference between counting a pile of coins left to right and sorting them by denomination first.

THE PAYOFF IS LIMITS. Lebesgue's convergence theorems say when the limit of integrals equals the integral of the limit, which Riemann's theory handles badly, and that is exactly what probability needs — Kolmogorov's axioms are these axioms normalised to total mass one.

It also finds its own edge: assuming the axiom of choice, NON-MEASURABLE sets exist (Vitali), sets so pathological that no consistent notion of size can be assigned. Not everything can be measured, and the theory is precise about which things cannot.

title: Statistical learning theory (bias-variance, generalization)
body:
Statistical learning theory (bias-variance, generalization) — an engine domain that can touch it: statistics. Calibration: map-only — bounds are asymptotic and assumption-laden. Why fitting the data you have is not the same as predicting the data you do not. Error decomposes into BIAS, from a model too simple to capture the pattern, and VARIANCE, from a model so flexible it fits the noise — and reducing one typically raises the other.

A model that fits the training data perfectly has usually memorised it, which is why generalisation must be measured on data held back and never touched. VC dimension makes model capacity quantitative and yields bounds on the gap between training and true error.

THE NO-FREE-LUNCH THEOREM is the honest floor under all of it: averaged over ALL possible problems, every learning algorithm performs identically. Any method that works does so because its assumptions match the structure of the world it is applied to — there is no assumption-free learner, and a system that claims to be one is hiding its priors rather than lacking them.

title: Mechanism design & auction theory
body:
Mechanism design & auction theory — an engine domain that can touch it: economics. Calibration: partial — auction outcomes and incentive conditions compute. Game theory run BACKWARDS: instead of asking what players will do given the rules, fix the outcome you want and design rules whose equilibrium produces it. Sometimes called reverse game theory, and it earned the 2007 Nobel.

INCENTIVE COMPATIBILITY is the goal — rules under which telling the truth is each participant's best move, so you need not detect lying because lying does not pay. The SECOND-PRICE (Vickrey) auction is the clean example: the highest bidder wins but pays the SECOND-highest bid, and under that rule bidding your true value is optimal regardless of what anyone else does. A small change in the rules removes the entire game of guessing.

OLDER AND SIMPLER: 'I cut, you choose' is mechanism design, and it makes fairness self-enforcing without a judge.

THE LIMITS ARE PROVED TOO, which keeps this honest. The Myerson-Satterthwaite theorem shows no mechanism can guarantee efficient trade between a buyer and seller with private values, budget balance and voluntary participation all at once. Some things cannot be designed around, and knowing which is part of the discipline.

title: Hermeneutics (the theory of interpretation)
body: Hermeneutics (the theory of interpretation) — an engine domain that can touch it: philosophy. Calibration: map-only — out of scope for sealing — foundational, empirical or interpretive (RESONANCE); for theology, CONCORDANT: a signpost, never HOLDS. How meaning is drawn from a text, and what makes one reading better than another. THE HERMENEUTICAL CIRCLE is its central finding: the parts are understood through the whole and the whole through the parts, so understanding is necessarily iterative — you arrive with a pre-understanding, the text corrects it, and you read again with the corrected one. THE SCHOOLS DISAGREE AND THE DISAGREEMENT IS KEPT: Alexandria (Origen) read allegorically for a spiritual sense beneath the letter, Antioch (Theodore, Chrysostom) held to the literal-historical sense; the Reformers held perspicuity and the grammatical-historical method — the text means what its author meant, in its language and its moment — against a reading secured by magisterium; the historical-critical school treats pre-understanding as contamination to be removed, while Gadamer answers that it is the very condition of understanding, and calls the goal a fusion of horizons. Ricoeur adds the hermeneutic of suspicion: ask what a text conceals as well as what it says. WHY IT BINDS HERE: every rule this library runs on is a hermeneutical commitment — original languages carry the authority, translation is a vehicle, a citation is not a proof, and authority is never silently upgraded by saving, repeating or hashing a claim. Kept as map-only: which reading is right is not a computation, and a tool that sealed an interpretation would be doing the reader's work and calling it verification.

title: Textual criticism (establishing what the text says)

title: Translation theory (formal vs dynamic equivalence)

title: Aperiodic tiling (Penrose, and the 2023 monotile)
body:
Two tile shapes plus local edge-matching rules that cover the plane completely and CANNOT repeat. Penrose (1974) gave two forms: P2, the kite and dart; P3, a thin rhombus (36°) and a fat one (72°). The rules are entirely local — each tile only constrains its immediate neighbours — yet they forbid any translational symmetry across the whole infinite plane.

TWO PROPERTIES CARRY THE WEIGHT. First, as a patch grows the ratio of fat tiles to thin converges to φ, the golden ratio, which is irrational — and an irrational ratio is precisely why no unit cell can ever close up and repeat. Second, every finite patch recurs infinitely often (repetitivity), so the tiling looks the same everywhere locally while never repeating globally. That is LONG-RANGE ORDER WITHOUT PERIODICITY, and it also exhibits five-fold symmetry, which the crystallographic restriction theorem proves impossible for any periodic lattice.

THE COUNT WAS NOT FUNDAMENTAL. In 2023 Smith, Myers, Kaplan and Goodman-Strauss found the 'hat', a SINGLE aperiodic monotile (using reflections), then 'Spectre', which is strictly chiral and needs none. So 'two tiles' was a bound on what had been imagined, not on the plane — a useful correction to keep on the card rather than in a footnote.

The honest calibration is map-only: specific relations here compute, but the classification of aperiodic tilings is not a sealable arithmetic claim.

title: Quasicrystals (forbidden symmetry in real matter)
body:
Matter that is ordered but not periodic. Dan Shechtman recorded an electron diffraction pattern from rapidly cooled Al-Mn on 8 April 1982 showing SHARP Bragg peaks with ten-fold symmetry — sharp peaks mean long-range order, and ten-fold symmetry is forbidden to any periodic lattice. Both at once was held to be impossible. He was told to go read a textbook and was asked to leave his research group; the result was published in 1984 and took the Nobel Prize in Chemistry in 2011.

THE RESOLUTION IS THE TILING. A quasicrystal is the physical realisation of an aperiodic tiling in three dimensions, and its diffraction pattern is the Fourier transform of that structure: a pure point spectrum — genuinely sharp peaks — arising from a structure with no repeating unit cell. Order and periodicity, which crystallography had treated as one idea, are two.

Quasicrystals were later found to occur naturally, in the Khatyrka meteorite (icosahedrite, reported 2009), so this is not only a laboratory artefact. The class is now standard: the International Union of Crystallography redefined 'crystal' in 1992 around discrete diffraction rather than around periodicity.

the entire evidence for a quasicrystal is a diffraction pattern, so the claim rests on diffraction theory: sharpness of the peaks measures the coherence length of the order, and their angular arrangement measures its symmetry. Change the optics and the finding evaporates

title: Girih tiles — quasi-periodic design in medieval Islamic architecture
body:
Girih are the polygonal tiles — decagon, pentagon, hexagon, bowtie, rhombus — carrying strapwork lines, used across medieval Islamic architecture. Peter Lu and Paul Steinhardt showed in Science (2007) that the tilework of the Darb-i Imam shrine at Isfahan (1453) forms a nearly perfect DECAGONAL QUASI-PERIODIC pattern, with the self-similar subdivision that generates it — roughly five centuries before Penrose described the mathematics.

THE METHOD IS THE POINT, AND IT IS AN ARCHITECTURAL ONE. At that scale the pattern cannot be laid out by straightedge and compass; the craftsmen worked by applying LOCAL tile rules and a subdivision recipe, and global quasi-periodic order followed without any global plan being drawn. The Topkapı Scroll records the design practice.

STATE THE LIMIT PLAINLY, because the claim is easy to overreach: this is not a proof that medieval architects possessed the modern theory, and the tilings are not perfect Penrose tilings — defects occur, and the interpretation has been contested. What is established is that the geometry was constructed and understood as a system, and that the same structure was reached by craft long before it was reached by proof.

title: Optimal packing & the honeycomb conjecture (Hales)
body:
The hexagonal grid is the most efficient way to divide a surface into regions of equal area with the LEAST TOTAL PERIMETER. Stated by Pappus of Alexandria around 300 AD as an observation about bees, it resisted proof for seventeen centuries; Thomas Hales proved it in 1999. The same author proved the Kepler conjecture on sphere packing (1998, formal verification completed 2014).

WHY A HEXAGON. Among regular polygons only the triangle, square and hexagon tile the plane, and of those the hexagon encloses the most area per unit of boundary — it is the closest a tile can get to a circle while still tiling without gaps. In a comb every wall is SHARED between two cells, so a hexagonal tiling costs exactly three walls per cell. That is the number to measure any cellular structure against.

THE CONTRAST WITH APERIODIC TILING IS THE USEFUL PART. A hexagonal comb is one tile, periodic, maximally efficient — and every cell is interchangeable, so the ARRANGEMENT carries no information. An aperiodic tiling pays slightly more and buys an arrangement that is itself information: infinitely many distinct patches, none repeating. Two answers to one question — how do you cover a plane — optimised for different things.

Calibration is `seals` because the geometric quantities here are computable: area, perimeter and the perimeter-to-area ratio of a regular polygon all verify directly.

title: Spectroscopy (how we know what a distant thing is made of)
body:
Spectroscopy (how we know what a distant thing is made of) — an engine domain that can touch it: optics. Calibration: seals — wavelengths, Doppler shifts and Wien's law all recompute and check. Split light into its wavelengths and a pattern of bright or dark lines appears. Each element produces a FIXED set of lines — a fingerprint that does not change with distance, temperature or motion, only its brightness and its position along the wavelength axis do.

THIS IS THE INSTRUMENT THAT MADE ASTRONOMY A PHYSICAL SCIENCE. Auguste Comte chose the chemical composition of stars in 1835 as his example of knowledge forever beyond reach; within about twenty-five years Kirchhoff and Bunsen were reading it off Fraunhofer's dark lines. Helium was found in the Sun's spectrum in 1868 before it was found on Earth, which is why it is named for helios.

THREE MEASUREMENTS COME OFF ONE SPECTRUM. Composition, from which lines are present. VELOCITY, from how far the whole pattern is Doppler-shifted — this is where redshift comes from, and therefore Hubble's law and the expansion. Temperature, from the shape of the continuum by Wien's displacement law. Nearly every astronomical claim on this floor secretly rests on this card, which is exactly why it was worth noticing that the corpus did not contain it.

The lines themselves are explained by quantum mechanics: an electron falling between allowed energy levels emits a photon of exactly that energy difference. Bohr's model gave the first quantitative account of the hydrogen series.

title: The electromagnetic spectrum & modulation (radio to gamma, one axis)
body:
The electromagnetic spectrum & modulation (radio to gamma, one axis) — an engine domain that can touch it: physics. Calibration: seals — c = fλ, photon energy E = hf, and bandwidth relations all recompute and check. Radio, microwave, infrared, visible light, ultraviolet, X-ray and gamma are ONE phenomenon at different frequencies, not seven phenomena. All travel at c; all obey c = fλ; all are solutions of Maxwell's equations. Visible light is about one octave of a spectrum spanning some twenty.

WHY THE BANDS LOOK DIFFERENT IS ABOUT ENERGY, NOT KIND: E = hf, so a gamma photon carries enough energy to break a molecule while a radio photon does not — the difference between ionising and non-ionising radiation is a number on one axis, not two categories.

MODULATION IS HOW INFORMATION RIDES A FREQUENCY. Amplitude modulation, the oldest form: s(t) = A[1 + μ·m(t)]·cos(2πf_c t), where f_c is the carrier, m(t) the message and μ ≤ 1 the modulation index. Multiplying two sinusoids produces sum and difference frequencies, so the spectrum of an AM signal is the carrier plus two mirror SIDEBANDS at f_c ± f_m — which is why a broadcast channel is twice the highest audio frequency (10 kHz channels for ~5 kHz audio).

AM'S TRADE IS THE INTERESTING PART. The carrier holds roughly two thirds of the transmitted power and carries NO information, which is grossly inefficient for the transmitter. It buys one thing: demodulation by ENVELOPE DETECTION — a diode and an RC network follow the outline of the wave, with no local oscillator, no phase lock and no clock recovery. That is why a crystal set (antenna, tuned coil, diode, earpiece) needs no battery at all: it runs on energy harvested from the wave itself. AM spends transmitter cost to make receivers nearly free and hard to switch off.

THE SAME AXIS READ THE OTHER WAY IS ASTRONOMY. A radio receiver tunes one frequency and rejects the rest; a spectrometer does exactly that across light. We modulate a carrier to impose information on it; a star's atmosphere modulates the continuum by absorbing at fixed frequencies, and spectroscopy reads that. AM sidebands and the Doppler broadening of a spectral line are the same mathematics on the same axis.

title: Spacetime & the quantum-gravity problem (where physics ends)
body:
Spacetime & the quantum-gravity problem (where physics ends) — an engine domain that can touch it: physics. Calibration: map-only — the Planck quantities compute, but there is no accepted theory here to seal, and saying so IS the content of this card.

TWO THEORIES, EACH SUPERBLY CONFIRMED, THAT CANNOT BOTH BE RIGHT. General relativity treats spacetime as smooth, dynamical, and curved by mass-energy. Quantum field theory treats fields as quantised and probabilistic on a FIXED background spacetime. Each is verified to extraordinary precision in its own regime, and their assumptions contradict one another where both must apply: inside a black hole, and at the first instant of the expansion.

THE FAILURE IS TECHNICAL AND SPECIFIC, not a matter of taste. Quantising gravity the way the other forces were quantised produces a NON-RENORMALIZABLE theory: the infinities cannot be absorbed into finitely many measured constants, so the method that succeeded for electromagnetism and the nuclear forces fails here. The scale where the conflict becomes unavoidable is Planck's: l_P = √(ħG/c³) ≈ 1.6×10⁻³⁵ m, some twenty orders of magnitude below anything a collider probes.

TWO SHARP SYMPTOMS. Singularities: general relativity outputs infinite curvature, and Penrose and Hawking proved these are generic. The black hole information paradox: Hawking radiation appears thermal, so information that fell in seems destroyed — which quantum mechanics forbids, since its evolution is unitary and reversible.

CANDIDATES EXIST AND NONE IS CONFIRMED: string theory, loop quantum gravity, causal set theory, asymptotic safety. None has made a tested prediction distinguishing it from the others. This card is deliberately map-only and deliberately present: a floor that cannot say where it ends is an idol, and this is the edge — the two best-tested descriptions of reality do not fit together, and nobody yet knows why.

title: Liebig's law of the minimum (what actually limits growth)
body:
Liebig's law of the minimum (what actually limits growth) — an engine domain that can touch it: soil_science. Calibration: seals — nutrient ratios and deficiency thresholds compute. Growth is limited by the SCARCEST necessary resource, not by the total amount of resources available. Justus von Liebig's image (1840) is a barrel made of staves of different heights: it holds water only to the shortest stave, and lengthening any other stave adds nothing.

THE PRACTICAL CONSEQUENCE IS THE WHOLE VALUE. A field short of phosphorus does not respond to more nitrogen; the money spent on nitrogen is wasted until phosphorus is fixed. Test first, then correct the deficit — which is why a soil test is the cheapest input a farmer ever buys. The primary macronutrients are nitrogen, phosphorus and potassium (N-P-K, the three numbers on every fertiliser bag), with calcium, magnesium and sulphur behind them and micronutrients such as zinc, boron and iron behind those.

THE PATTERN GENERALISES far beyond soil: a system's throughput is set by its binding constraint, and effort spent anywhere else is absorbed without effect. That is the same shape as the bottleneck in a production line and the rate-determining step in a reaction.

title: Haber–Bosch nitrogen fixation (bread from air)
body:
Haber–Bosch nitrogen fixation (bread from air) — an engine domain that can touch it: chemistry. Calibration: seals — stoichiometry, yield and equilibrium shifts compute. N₂ + 3H₂ ⇌ 2NH₃, run at roughly 400-500°C and 150-300 atmospheres over an iron catalyst. Fritz Haber found the conditions (1909); Carl Bosch made them work at industrial scale (1913).

WHY THE BRUTAL CONDITIONS: the nitrogen triple bond is one of the strongest in chemistry, so the reaction is slow. Heat speeds it but, being exothermic, heat also shifts the equilibrium BACKWARD by Le Chatelier's principle — so the process runs at a deliberately compromised temperature and recovers the loss with enormous pressure and catalysis. It is the textbook case of engineering against an equilibrium rather than with it.

THE CONSEQUENCE IS DEMOGRAPHIC. Before this, usable nitrogen came from manure, legumes, and mined guano and nitrate; the supply was hard-capped. Roughly half the nitrogen atoms in a living human body today passed through this process, and it is commonly credited with supporting about half the world's present population. It consumes on the order of 1-2% of world energy.

IT IS ALSO DUAL-USE AND THE CARD SAYS SO: fixed nitrogen makes fertiliser and it makes explosives, and the same chemistry sustained the German war effort after 1914. Haber directed chemical-weapons work in that war. The runoff cost is real too — nitrate leaching, algal blooms and coastal dead zones. A technology can feed billions and poison estuaries with the same molecule.

title: The Green Revolution (Borlaug, semi-dwarf breeding)
body:
The Green Revolution (Borlaug, semi-dwarf breeding) — an engine domain that can touch it: agriculture. Calibration: map-only — yields are historical measurements, not a sealable computation. Norman Borlaug bred wheat that was disease-resistant, photoperiod-insensitive and — the decisive trait — SEMI-DWARF.

THE DWARFING IS THE INSIGHT, AND IT IS MECHANICAL. Fertilising a traditional tall wheat makes it grow tall and fall over under the weight of its own grain, so the extra nitrogen is lost to lodging. A short stiff stalk can carry a heavy head, so it converts fertiliser into grain instead of straw. Semi-dwarf varieties are what make Haber–Bosch nitrogen worth applying; neither achieves much without the other.

Mexico became wheat self-sufficient by 1956; India and Pakistan roughly doubled output in the late 1960s against confident predictions of mass famine. Borlaug took the Nobel Peace Prize in 1970 and is often credited with averting a billion deaths.

THE COSTS ARE PART OF THE RECORD. The package requires fertiliser, irrigation and often pesticide, so it favours farmers who can buy inputs and can deepen inequality; monoculture narrows the genetic base and raises epidemic risk; and irrigation has drawn down aquifers. This card is map-only because 'was it worth it' is not a computation — but the yields, and the costs, are both measured.

title: Crop rotation & biological nitrogen fixation (the low-input path)
body:
Crop rotation & biological nitrogen fixation (the low-input path) — an engine domain that can touch it: agriculture. Calibration: map-only — rotation effects are empirical; nutrient budgets compute. Legumes — beans, peas, clover, lentils, groundnuts — host Rhizobium bacteria in root nodules, and those bacteria break the atmospheric nitrogen triple bond at ordinary soil temperature using the nitrogenase enzyme. What Haber–Bosch needs 400°C and 200 atmospheres to do, a root nodule does in a field, for free.

THE NORFOLK FOUR-COURSE (wheat, turnips, barley, clover) spread in 18th-century Britain and eliminated the fallow year: the clover restored nitrogen while feeding livestock, whose manure returned more. Rotation also breaks pest and disease cycles, since a pathogen specialised on one crop starves when the field changes.

THIS IS THE CARD THAT MATTERS MOST TO A FARMER WITH NO CASH. The Green Revolution package assumes purchased inputs. Rotation, intercropping and cover crops buy fertility with knowledge and labour instead of money, and they are available to a smallholder with no supply chain, no credit and no fuel. Lower ceiling than industrial nitrogen, far lower floor of dependency — and the two can be combined rather than chosen between.

title: Vaccination & immune memory (Jenner to eradication)
body:
Vaccination & immune memory (Jenner to eradication) — an engine domain that can touch it: medicine. Calibration: map-only — herd-immunity thresholds compute; efficacy is empirical. Show the immune system a harmless likeness of a pathogen and it remembers, so the real encounter meets a defence already prepared. Edward Jenner (1796) observed that milkmaids who caught cowpox did not get smallpox, and deliberately inoculated with the milder disease — vacca is Latin for cow, which is where the word comes from.

THE MECHANISM, FOUND LATER, IS ADAPTIVE IMMUNITY: B and T cells that recognise a specific antigen proliferate, and a subset persists for years as MEMORY cells, so the second response is faster and stronger than the first. This is the immune system learning from a sample — the same shape as any system that generalises from examples.

SMALLPOX IS THE PROOF: declared eradicated in 1980, the only human disease ever eliminated from the world. Rinderpest followed in cattle.

HERD IMMUNITY IS A COMPUTATION, not an opinion: the fraction that must be immune to stop sustained transmission is about 1 - 1/R₀, so a disease with R₀ = 12 like measles needs roughly 92% coverage and one with R₀ = 3 needs about 67%. That threshold is why coverage gaps matter to people who cannot be vaccinated — infants, the immunosuppressed — and it is arithmetic rather than exhortation.

title: Antisepsis & handwashing (Semmelweis, Lister)
body:
Antisepsis & handwashing (Semmelweis, Lister) — an engine domain that can touch it: medicine. Calibration: map-only — the effect sizes are historical measurements. Ignaz Semmelweis noticed in 1847 that the Vienna maternity ward staffed by doctors killed mothers at roughly three times the rate of the ward staffed by midwives. The doctors came from autopsies. He ordered handwashing in chlorinated lime, and mortality on that ward fell from about 18% to around 2%.

HE WAS REJECTED, and the reason is worth keeping: he had a decisive measurement and no mechanism, germ theory being twenty years away, and his claim implied that respectable physicians were killing their patients. He was dismissed, deteriorated, and died in an asylum in 1865. Joseph Lister, working from Pasteur, introduced carbolic acid antisepsis in 1867 and was believed, because by then there was a theory to hang the fact on.

THIS IS THE CHEAPEST HIGH-VALUE INTERVENTION IN MEDICINE and it still is: soap, clean water and the discipline to use them before touching a patient or food. It requires no supply chain beyond soap, which is exactly why it belongs in a field library.

The methodological lesson is on the card deliberately: a measured effect with no mechanism is still evidence, and demanding a mechanism before acting on a clear result cost thousands of lives here.

title: Antibiotics & antimicrobial resistance (Fleming's own warning)
body:
Antibiotics & antimicrobial resistance (Fleming's own warning) — an engine domain that can touch it: medicine. Calibration: map-only — dosing computes (see pharmacokinetics); resistance dynamics are empirical. Alexander Fleming returned from holiday in 1928 to a contaminated culture plate on which a Penicillium mould had cleared a ring in the surrounding bacteria. He identified the cause and could not purify it; Howard Florey and Ernst Chain turned it into a usable drug in the early 1940s, and the three shared the 1945 Nobel.

RESISTANCE IS NOT MISUSE OF THE THEORY, IT IS THE THEORY. An antibiotic is a selection pressure: the susceptible die, any resistant variant survives and reproduces, and the population shifts. This is Darwinian evolution running on a timescale of days, observable in a hospital ward. Fleming said so in his own 1945 Nobel lecture, warning that under-dosing would breed resistant strains.

THE PRACTICE THAT FOLLOWS IS SPECIFIC: antibiotics do nothing against viruses, so taking them for a cold buys no benefit and pays the full cost in selection; and a course must be taken as prescribed, because stopping when symptoms ease leaves the hardiest survivors to repopulate. Routine use as a growth promoter in livestock is the largest single driver worldwide.

title: Sanitation, clean water & oral rehydration (Snow's pump handle)
body:
Sanitation, clean water & oral rehydration (Snow's pump handle) — an engine domain that can touch it: medicine. Calibration: seals — ORS composition and dilution compute exactly. In the 1854 Soho cholera outbreak John Snow mapped the deaths, found them clustered around the Broad Street pump, and had the handle removed. Cholera was waterborne, not carried on bad air — and he showed it with a map and a count, before anyone had seen the bacterium. This is the founding act of epidemiology: a spatial pattern in data can identify a cause that no microscope has yet resolved.

SEPARATING DRINKING WATER FROM SEWAGE has saved more lives than any drug ever invented. It is civil engineering doing medicine's work, and it is the reason the great cholera and typhoid epidemics ended in cities that built it.

ORAL REHYDRATION IS THE FIELD-LEVEL COMPANION AND IT COMPUTES. Cholera kills by dehydration, not by the organism itself, and the discovery that glucose drives sodium co-transport across the intestinal wall EVEN WHILE it is inflamed means fluid can be replaced by mouth. The WHO formulation is roughly one level teaspoon of salt and six of sugar in one litre of clean water — ingredients a household already has. Deployed from the 1970s, ORS cut cholera case fatality from around 30% to under 1% and is credited with tens of millions of children's lives. The Lancet called it potentially the most important medical advance of the century, and it costs pennies.

title: Electromagnetic induction (Faraday's law — how all electricity is made)
body:
Electromagnetic induction (Faraday's law — how all electricity is made) — an engine domain that can touch it: electrical. Calibration: seals — EMF, turns ratio and flux relations compute. A CHANGING magnetic flux through a circuit induces a voltage: EMF = -dΦ/dt. Michael Faraday demonstrated it in 1831 with a coil, a magnet and a galvanometer.

THE WORD 'CHANGING' IS THE ENTIRE CONTENT. A stationary magnet in a coil induces nothing; motion or variation is required, which is why generators rotate and why transformers work only on alternating current. The minus sign is Lenz's law: the induced current opposes the change that produced it, which is conservation of energy showing up as a sign — if it added instead of opposed, you could crank a generator and get free energy.

ESSENTIALLY ALL ELECTRICITY IN THE WORLD IS MADE BY THIS ONE EFFECT. Coal, gas, nuclear, hydro, wind and geothermal differ only in what spins the shaft; the shaft turns a conductor in a field and the field does the rest. Run it backwards and it is a motor. Wind two coils on one core and it is a transformer, which is what makes long-distance power transmission possible at all.

title: AC & the polyphase system (Tesla, and why the grid is alternating)
body:
AC & the polyphase system (Tesla, and why the grid is alternating) — an engine domain that can touch it: electrical. Calibration: seals — transmission loss, turns ratio and phase relations compute. Nikola Tesla's contribution is usually told as a personality contest and is actually an engineering argument that has a right answer.

TRANSMISSION LOSS IS I²R. Power delivered is V×I, so the same power can be sent at high voltage and low current or the reverse — and since loss goes as the SQUARE of current, raising voltage tenfold cuts losses a hundredfold. Only alternating current can be stepped up and down efficiently, by a transformer, which needs a changing flux to work. That is why Edison's DC scheme required a generating station every mile or so and why the grid is AC.

THE ROTATING MAGNETIC FIELD (1887) is the deeper idea: feed three coils spaced 120° apart with three currents 120° out of phase and the resulting field ROTATES with no moving contacts. That gives the induction motor — no brushes, no commutator, nothing to wear out — which is still the workhorse of nearly every pump, fan and machine tool in the world.

The Tesla coil is a resonant air-core transformer: two LC circuits tuned to the same frequency so energy transfers efficiently between them, which is the same resonance principle a radio receiver uses to select one station out of the spectrum.

title: Fluid mechanics (Bernoulli, Reynolds, Navier–Stokes)
body:
Fluid mechanics (Bernoulli, Reynolds, Navier–Stokes) — an engine domain that can touch it: hydrology. Calibration: seals — continuity, Bernoulli and Reynolds number compute directly. CONTINUITY first: what flows in must flow out, so narrowing a pipe speeds the flow. BERNOULLI second: along a streamline, pressure plus kinetic plus potential energy is constant, so where a fluid speeds up its pressure DROPS — which is a statement of energy conservation, not a special force.

REYNOLDS NUMBER decides the character of the flow: Re = ρvL/μ, the ratio of inertial to viscous forces. Below roughly 2,300 in a pipe the flow is LAMINAR, orderly and predictable; above about 4,000 it is TURBULENT, chaotic and mixing, with far higher drag and heat transfer. One dimensionless number tells you which world you are in, and it is why a small model in a wind tunnel can predict a full-size aircraft — match the Reynolds number and the physics matches.

NAVIER–STOKES is the full equation set, and whether smooth solutions always exist in three dimensions is an open Clay Millennium Problem. We design aircraft, pipelines and heart valves with equations whose basic mathematical behaviour is unproven — an honest thing for the floor to record.

title: Heat transfer (conduction, convection, radiation)
body:
Heat transfer (conduction, convection, radiation) — an engine domain that can touch it: thermodynamics. Calibration: seals — Fourier's law, R-values and Stefan–Boltzmann all compute. Heat moves three ways and only three. CONDUCTION through touching matter, Fourier's law: rate ∝ area × temperature difference ÷ thickness. CONVECTION by bulk movement of a fluid, which is why a draught chills and why hot air rises. RADIATION as electromagnetic waves needing no medium at all, rising as the FOURTH POWER of absolute temperature (Stefan–Boltzmann) — which is why a fire warms your face across a room and why a clear night sky freezes a crop even in still air.

THE PRACTICAL READING IS DIRECT AND IT IS WHY THIS CARD BELONGS IN A FIELD LIBRARY. Insulation fights conduction, and its R-value is thickness over conductivity. Sealing gaps fights convection, and is usually cheaper per degree than adding insulation. Foil and light colours fight radiation. Thermal mass does not stop heat, it DELAYS it — a thick wall shifts the afternoon peak into the evening, which is the whole logic of adobe and stone building in hot dry climates.

All three run only from hot to cold on their own, which is the second law setting the direction.
